newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries tread water in London before sales data.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries tread water in London before sales data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were steady in slack London trade on Tuesday and dealers said there was little prospect of a boost to the market from key June retail sales data due later.

"A lot of the good news is priced in to the market now -- the retail sales numbers will have to be very weak if we're going to see much of a rally from current levels," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at Bank America in London.

He said the data would probably be consistent with tentative indications that U.S. consumers are starting to spend again. "But there will be no evidence consumption is going to grow at a rate which will concern the Fed," Hawkins added.

According to a Reuters poll, economists expect U.S. retail sales to rise 0.2 percent in June after falling 0.1 percent in May. Excluding autos, they see sales up 0.5 percent after their 0.1 percent May fall.

Hawkins said the data was unlikely to impact on interest rate expectations for the August Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, but added the market should be wary of any revisions to back data.
"A moderate gain in non-autos plus a positive back revision won't convince the Fed to tighten in August but it may raise alarm bells for the September FOMC," he said.

"The market looks relatively comfortably priced, and with PPI tomorrow which is expected to underline the benign inflation picture, even if today's numbers are firm, it won't necessarily mean the market will fall out of bed," he added.

By 0955 GMT, the 30-year cash bond was at 100-25, to yield 6.56 percent, up from 100-24 in Tokyo and down from 100-29 at the New York close. The 10-year paper was at 102-17, down from 102-18 in Tokyo and 102-22 in New York.
One dealer said there had been some swap trading in three and five year notes but added on the whole the market was very quiet.
"I'd be a seller of strength -- the market is running out of gas and there's quite a bit of resistance at the 6.5 percent yield level on the 30-year," he said.

Hawkins noted the strong performance by the dollar had had little impact on the Treasury market, but if anything, was broadly supportive. By 1000 GMT, dollar/yen was at 114.38/48 and dollar/mark was at 1.7948/53.
The September T-bond future was down 8/32 at 113-22 in automated trade.
